arxiv-2104-01920.title: Adjusted composite likelihood for robust Bayesian meta-analysis
arxiv-2104-01920.creator: Michele Lambardi di San Miniato, Nicola Sartori
arxiv-2104-01920.description: Abstract A composite likelihood is a non-genuine likelihood function that allows to make inference on limited aspects of a model, such as marginal or conditional distributions. Composite likelihoods are not proper likelihoods and need therefore calibration for their use in inference, from both a frequentist and a Bayesian perspective.

arxiv-2110-15632.title: Bayesian Optimal Experimental Design for Simulator Models of Cognition
arxiv-2110-15632.creator: Simon Valentin, Steven Kleinegesse, Neil R. Bramley, Michael U. Gutmann, Christopher G. Lucas
arxiv-2110-15632.description: Abstract Bayesian optimal experimental design (BOED) is a methodology to identify experiments that are expected to yield informative data. Recent work in cognitive science considered BOED for computational models of human behavior with tractable and known likelihood functions. However, tractability often comes at the cost of realism; simulator models that can capture the richness of human behavior are often intractable.

arxiv-2112-06766.title: Majorana zero modes induced by superconducting phase bias
arxiv-2112-06766.creator: Yuval Oreg
arxiv-2112-06766.description: Abstract Majorana zero modes in condensed matter systems have been the subject of much interest in recent years. Their non-Abelian exchange statistics, making them a unique state of matter, and their potential applications in topological quantum computation, earned them attention from both theorists and experimentalists.

arxiv-2203-08794.title: Double sweep LU decomposition for American options under negative rates
arxiv-2203-08794.creator: Fabien Le Floc’h
arxiv-2203-08794.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Fabien Le Floc’h. The classic Brennan-Schwartz algorithm to solve the linear complementary problem, which arises from the finite difference discretization of the partial differential equation related to American option pricing does not lead to the exact solution under negative interest rates. This is due to the two exercise boundaries which may appear under negative interest rate, while the algorithm was proven to lead to the exact solution in the case of a single exercise boundary only.

arxiv-2204-02751.title: Influence of spin-orbit coupling on chemical bonding
arxiv-2204-02751.creator: Andris Gulans 1,2, Claudia Draxl 2
arxiv-2204-02751.description: Abstract The influence of spin-orbit interaction on chemical bonds in elemental solids and homonuclear dimers is analyzed by means of density-functional-theory calculations. Employing highly precise all-electron full-potential methodology, our results represent benchmark quality. Comparison of the scalar- and fully-relativistic approaches for elemental solids shows that the spin-orbit interaction may contract or expand the volume of the considered material.

arxiv-2312-12592.title: Three Point Amplitudes in Matrix Theory
arxiv-2312-12592.description: Abstract Aidan Herderschee and Juan Maldacena Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, NJ 08540, USA We compute the three graviton amplitude in the Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind matrix model for M-theory. Even though the three point amplitude is determined by super Poincare invariance in eleven dimensional M-theory, it requires a non-trivial computation in the matrix model.

arxiv-2404-02418.title: Auxiliary task demands mask the capabilities of smaller language models
arxiv-2404-02418.creator: Jennifer Hu, Michael C. Frank
arxiv-2404-02418.description: Abstract Developmental psychologists have argued about when cognitive capacities such as language understanding or theory of mind emerge. These debates often hinge on the concept of “task demands” – the auxiliary challenges associated with performing a particular evaluation – that may mask the child’s underlying ability.

arxiv-2404-10790.title: Multimodal Attack Detection for Action Recognition Models
arxiv-2404-10790.creator: Furkan Mumcu, Yasin Yilmaz
arxiv-2404-10790.description: Abstract Adversarial machine learning attacks on video action recognition models is a growing research area and many effective attacks were introduced in recent years. These attacks show that action recognition models can be breached in many ways. Hence using these models in practice raises significant security concerns.

arxiv-2406-10998.title: History-enhanced ICT For Sustainability education: Learning together with Business Computing students. Thanks: The research was part-funded by the Royal Historical Society through the award of a Jinty Nelson Teaching Fellowship 2023-24 to the research team.
arxiv-2406-10998.creator: Ian Brooks, Laura Harrison, Mark Reeves, Martin Simpson, Rose Wallis
arxiv-2406-10998.description: Abstract This research explores the use of History to enhance education in the field of ICT For Sustainability (ICT4S) in response to a challenge from the ICT4S 2023 conference. No previous studies were found in ICT4S but the literature on History and Education for Sustainable Development is reviewed.

arxiv-2407-07726.title: PaliGemma: A versatile 3B VLM for transfer
arxiv-2407-07726.creator: Lucas Beyer, Andreas Steiner, André Susano Pinto, Alexander Kolesnikov, Xiao Wang, Daniel Salz, Maxim Neumann, Ibrahim Alabdulmohsin, Michael Tschannen, Emanuele Bugliarello, Thomas Unterthiner, Daniel Keysers, Skanda Koppula, Fangyu Liu, Adam Grycner, Alexey Gritsenko, Neil Houlsby, Manoj Kumar, Ke
arxiv-2407-07726.description: Abstract PaliGemma is an open Vision-Language Model (VLM) that is based on the SigLIP-So400m vision encoder and the Gemma-2B language model. It is trained to be a versatile and broadly knowledgeable base model that is effective to transfer. It achieves strong performance on a wide variety of open-world tasks.

arxiv-2409-14175.title: QMOS: Enhancing LLMs for Telecommunication with Question Masked loss and Option Shuffling * These authors contributed equally to this work. ** Mentor of the Team.
arxiv-2409-14175.creator: Blessed Guda * , Gabrial Zencha Ashungafac * , Lawrence Francis * , Carlee Joe-Wong **
arxiv-2409-14175.description: Abstract Large Language models (LLMs) have brought about substantial advancements in the field of Question Answering (QA) systems. These models do remarkably well in addressing intricate inquiries in a variety of disciplines. However, because of domain-specific vocabulary, complex technological concepts, and the requirement for exact responses, applying LLMs to specialized sectors like telecommunications presents additional obstacles. arxiv-2412-16928.title: AV-DTEC: Self-Supervised Audio-Visual Fusion for Drone Trajectory Estimation and Classification
arxiv-2412-16928.creator: Zhenyuan Xiao, Yizhuo Yang, Guili Xu*, Xianglong Zeng, Shenghai Yuan
arxiv-2412-16928.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhenyuan Xiao, Yizhuo Yang, Guili Xu*, Xianglong Zeng, Shenghai Yuan. The increasing use of compact UAVs has created significant threats to public safety, while traditional drone detection systems are often bulky and costly. To address these challenges, we propose AV-DTEC, a lightweight self-supervised audio-visual fusion-based anti-UAV system. AV-DTEC is trained using self-supervised learning with labels generated by LiDAR, and it simultaneously learns audio and visual features through a parallel selective state-space model.

arxiv-2502-02192.title: Topological Josephson vortices at finite voltage bias
arxiv-2502-02192.creator: Kiryl Piasotski, Adrian Reich, Alexander Shnirman
arxiv-2502-02192.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kiryl Piasotski, Adrian Reich, Alexander Shnirman. We study the effects of finite voltage bias on Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon (CdGM) states in topological Josephson junctions with a vortex lattice. The voltage drives vortices into steady motion, squeezing the CdGM spectrum due to quasi-relativistic dispersion. A finite voltage range allows well-defined states, but beyond a critical breakdown voltage, the states collapse to zero energy and become sharply localized, marking a dynamical transition. Additionally, finite bias modifies selection rules for CdGM state transitions.

pmc-10736478.title: MINORITY STRESS AND LONELINESS IN A LIFESPAN SAMPLE OF SEXUAL MINORITIES
pmc-10736478.creator: Michael Vale
pmc-10736478.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Marginalized individuals often experience social isolation (i.e., loneliness), which is a risk factor for diminished health, especially for older sexual minorities (i.e., LGB+) who were socialized in a period with less social recognition and overt stigmatization (i.e., minority stress). Although it is known that minority stressors contribute to loneliness, little is known about the contextual factors that predict this relationship, such as age/cohort.

pmc-11333559.title: Developing Knowledge of Autism in Majority World Countries: Examples of Bolivia and Paraguay
pmc-11333559.creator: Carol Westby, Rosario Roman
pmc-11333559.description: Bolivia and Paraguay are Majority World countries, which are defined as areas within which most of the world’s population live, natural resources and landmass are located, but are often economically poor. Minority world countries, such as, the United States, have a smaller percentage of the world’s population, but often a greater share of the world’s wealth.

pmc-11406811.title: Folliculocentric tinea versicolor: a case report
pmc-11406811.creator: Ruili Jiang, Yun Xia, Bei Wang, Zilu Qu, Liuqing Chen, Feng Hu
pmc-11406811.description: BackgroundTinea versicolor is a very common condition. We reported a specific follicular manifestation and proposed that this particular presentation might be related to the patient’s history of previous keratosis pilaris.Case presentationA 46-year-old Asian woman of Han ethnicity presented to the clinic with trunk lesions for over a year.

pmc-11518271.title: Heterogeneity in health and lifestyle among preschool children with migrant background in Sweden
pmc-11518271.creator: S Alseddig, F K Nkulu Kalengayi, M Vaezghasemi, L Lundahl, M Lindkvist, K Lindvall, S A Silfverdal, A Ivarsson
pmc-11518271.description: BackgroundParental country of birth and socioeconomic status affect children’s health, lifestyle, and access to care. But inequality patterns may vary depending on the outcome and indicator being studied. While prior studies have focused on single health outcomes, this study assessed the relationship between parental migrant status and a range of health and lifestyle indicators among 3-year-old children.

pmc-12382196.title: Women’s experiences of changes in related men’s impulsivity and domestic violence following men’s participation in the ReINVEST clinical trial
pmc-12382196.creator: Amanuel Kidane Hagos, Eden Thain, Sarah Cox, Lee Knight, Peter Schofield, Tony Butler
pmc-12382196.description: BackgroundImpulsivity, a behaviour often associated with reactive violence to perceived provocation or stress is a key risk factor for Domestic Violence (DV) perpetration. This study explores the experiences of women on related men’s changes in impulsivity and DV following men’s participation in the ReINVEST clinical trial that investigated whether the commonly used antidepressant sertraline would reduce impulsivity and domestic violence.

pmc-12651872.title: An Interprofessional Training Ward in Pediatric Cardiology: Ensuring Patient Safety and Results from the Evaluation of Patient and Parent Satisfaction
pmc-12651872.creator: Anthea Peters, Wiebke Spree, Tobias Kratz, Soyhan Bagci, Johannes Breuer, Ageliki A Karatza
pmc-12651872.description: Background/Objectives: Interprofessional training wards (ITWs) are effective in fostering interprofessional collaboration during undergraduate medical training. Ensuring safety is particularly crucial for vulnerable patient groups. We developed a safety concept for the pediatric cardiology ITW, enabling nursing trainees and final-year medical students to independently care for children with congenital heart defects (CHDs).

pmc-12661390.title: Management of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis in Intensive Care Units: Guidelines From the Fungal Infection Network of Switzerland (FUNGINOS)
pmc-12661390.creator: F Lamoth, W C Albrich, S Ragozzino, D Bosetti, J Delaloye, C El Khoury, A Munting, V Portillo, I Reinhold, J Sumer, A Zbinden, V Bättig, C Beigelman‐Aubry, K Boggian, A Conen, T S Fischer, C Garzoni, D Goldenberger, E Hofmann, P Khafagy, L Kern, G R Kleger, C Le Terrier, O Marchetti, J L Pagani, N J
pmc-12661390.description: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is increasingly recognised in intensive care units (ICU) affecting not only patients with classical immunosuppressive conditions but also other severely ill patients, including those with respiratory viral infections (influenza, COVID‐19), advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or acute and chronic liver diseases. Several expert panels have proposed definitions of IPA in different ICU settings.

pmc-12748680.title: Prospective evaluation of speech as a digital biomarker for covert hepatic encephalopathy
pmc-12748680.creator: Jakub Gazda, Juan Carlos García-Pagán, Sylvia Drazilova, Peter Drotar, Mate Hires, Matej Gazda, Martin Janicko, Anna Baiges, Peter Jarcuska
pmc-12748680.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Covert hepatic encephalopathy is a highly prevalent complication of liver failure or portosystemic shunting. However, the current diagnostic methods have not been widely adopted in routine clinical practice due to their time-consuming or technically complex nature. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a clinically feasible machine learning model capable of detecting covert hepatic encephalopathy using features extracted from sustained vowel phonation recordings.

pmc-12965320.title: Neurons with granulovacuolar degeneration bodies are resilient to tau-induced protein synthesis impairment
pmc-12965320.creator: Jasper F. M. Smits, Thijmen W. Ligthart, Marta Jorge-Oliva, Skip Middelhoff, Fleur Schipper, Débora Pita-Illobre, Ka Wan Li, Wiep Scheper
pmc-12965320.description: In Alzheimer’s disease, many surviving neurons with tau pathology contain granulovacuolar degeneration bodies (GVBs), neuron-specific lysosomal structures induced by pathological tau assemblies. This could indicate a neuroprotective role for GVBs; however, the mechanism of GVB formation and its functional implications are elusive. Here, we demonstrate that casein kinase 1δ (CK1δ) activity is required for GVB formation.

pmc-13037314.title: Reactive thrombocytosis in hospitalized pneumonia reflects intense inflammation and confers context-dependent mortality risk
pmc-13037314.creator: Cheng Liu, Lili He, Yuanhao Guo, Yang Su, Yao Wei, Yongxin Li, Xiaolong Ma, Rui Qiao
pmc-13037314.description: BackgroundBeyond hemostasis, platelets’ immune and inflammatory role is recognized and thrombocytosis is generally regarded as a marker of the inflammatory response. However, the immune functions of platelets remain beneath the surface, and previous studies have reported conflicting findings regarding the significance of thrombocytosis in infection-related diseases. Can reactive thrombocytosis be viewed as a “higher-is-worse or higher-is-better” predictor of clinical outcome?

pmc-13199887.title: Bidirectional reallocations of sitting time, physical activity, and sleep in relation to risk of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular disease: An analysis of the Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology (PURE)-China cohort study
pmc-13199887.creator: Yilin Huang, Jun Hao, Bo Hu, Yang Wang, Lap Ah Tse, Weida Liu, Qiujing Cai, Biyan Wang, Zhiguang Liu, Tong Bu, Sumathy Rangarajan, Scott A. Lear, Wei Li, PURE-China Investigators
pmc-13199887.description: Highlights•A J-shaped association between daily sitting time and risks of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular disease was found in the PURE-China cohort, with increased risks at both low and high sitting levels.•Reallocating 30 min of sitting to physical activity in individuals sitting ≥4 h/day linked to 3–4%% lower composite outcome risk and 6%–7% lower all-cause mortality.

pmc-13251662.title: Vitamin D status and sarcopenia in older adults: population-based evidence for synergy with diabetes and experimental validation in an aged diabetic rat model
pmc-13251662.creator: Cheng Zhang, Mingkai Li, Chenyang Li, Lushan Xue, Chenhui Lv, Qinfei Guo, Yafei Zhao, Haifeng Zhao
pmc-13251662.description: Graphical abstractKeywords: Vitamin D deficiency, Sarcopenia, Diabetes, Older adults Introduction Sarcopenia is a geriatric syndrome characterized by accelerated loss of skeletal muscle mass and function and is closely associated with multiple adverse health outcomes [1]. As global population aging accelerates, sarcopenia has emerged as a major public health challenge that undermines physical function and quality of life in later life.

pmc-13306553.title: Advanced Antibacterial Nanocomposite Fibers for Biomedical Applications
pmc-13306553.creator: Francisca Acevedo, Manuel Azocar, Eulàlia Sans-Serramitjana, Jeyson Hermosilla, Felipe Gálvez-Jirón, Denisse Bravo, Dayaimi Gonzalez, Gabriela Guajardo, Cristóbal Guajardo, Rodrigo Navia
pmc-13306553.description: Background/Objectives: Wound infections represent a major clinical challenge due to their polymicrobial nature, biofilm formation, and increasing antimicrobial resistance, which compromise conventional treatments. This study aimed to develop and evaluate ligand-stabilized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) with improved antimicrobial activity and cytocompatibility, and to investigate their incorporation into electrospun nanofibers for wound management.

pmc-13316127.title: Chronic Expanding Hematoma Complicated by Life Threatening Hemoptysis and Respiratory Arrest—A Case Report
pmc-13316127.creator: Anthony Shing‐yiu Yu, Chung Yin Cheung, Chor Ting Ng, Chi Ching Chan, Ying Fung Lo, Judianna Suet Ying Yu, Wallace Hon Cheung Fan, Alwin Wai Tak Yeung
pmc-13316127.description: Chronic expanding hematoma (CEH) is a rare, indolent entity mostly linked to prior tuberculosis, thoracic surgery or trauma, with gradual long‐term enlargement and potentially fatal complications. We present a 73‐year‐old Nepalese male without classic predisposing risk factors, presenting with mild hemoptysis in 2017 and a large right pleural hematoma on computed tomography (CT).

pmc-13422442.title: Enhancing tobacco quality through microbial-enzymatic processing: mechanisms, applications, and future perspectives
pmc-13422442.creator: Lei Xu, Peng Zhang, Hui Zhang, Ping-Ping Liu, Zhe Jin, Jin-Song Gong, Zhen-Ming Lu, Qing-Xia Zheng, Guo-Yun Xu, Niu Zhai, Hui-Na Zhou, Yu-E. Li, Li-Feng Jin
pmc-13422442.description: Aging represents a critical stage in tobacco processing that balances the internal chemical composition of tobacco leaves, reduces undesirable odors and irritation, and enhances smoking quality. Microbial fermentation and enzymatic catalysis are pivotal to this process, as they not only accelerate the fermentation period but also regulate the internal chemical constituents of the leaves, thereby improving aging efficiency.

pmc-13476999.title: Simulation-based modeling of aortic valve neocuspidization with oversized pericardial leaflets
pmc-13476999.creator: Jalal Cherkaoui, Ines A Martínez, Yassine Toufique, James D St Louis, Mohammed Cherkaoui, Ignacio Lugones
pmc-13476999.description: ObjectiveAortic valve replacement in children is challenging. The lack of accommodation for somatic growth negatively impacts long-term outcomes. Data on the use of symmetrical oversized leaflets in neocuspidization are limited. We present a computer-based simulation of patient growth after a replacement with an oversized aortic valve leaflet.MethodsA new aortic valve design was modeled in silico.

pmc-13633842.title: Outcomes Following Single-Level Spinal Fusion in Patients With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
pmc-13633842.creator: Patrizia M Manziano, Grace Wilsey, Sarah Kebaish, Ved Vengsarkar, Joyce En-Hua Wang, Madison Sroufe, Kara McConaghy, Wendy Novicoff, Xudong Li, Stephen D Lockey
pmc-13633842.description: IntroductionPatients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) experience an increased risk of complications and healthcare expenditures after surgery, yet there is limited knowledge regarding outcomes after spinal fusion. This study aimed to investigate outcomes after single-level cervical and lumbar fusion in patients with SLE.
